## Field

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/field.html

Label, control, hint and error message wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-field` on the wrapper, `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"` on the messages

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/field.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/field.css):

```text
data-field              on the wrapper (a <div>, or a <fieldset> for groups)
data-field="hint"       on the hint
data-field="error"      on the error message
```

`data-field` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** the field's error text starts with the word "Error:" in the markup, rather than a CSS icon, so every user and every screen reader gets it with no extra API. Invalid controls also get a thick start border, a shape change as well as a color change.
- **Our choice:** a field is an atom here, not a molecule, because a control is not usable without its label, hint and error. Larger compositions (forms, cards, headers) are molecules and organisms for later milestones.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/field.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/field.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/field.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### With a hint

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-name">Display name</label>
  <input id="f-name" name="display-name" type="text" autocomplete="nickname" aria-describedby="f-name-hint">
  <p id="f-name-hint" data-field="hint">Shown next to your comments.</p>
</div>
```

#### With a hint and an error

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-email">Email</label>
  <input id="f-email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" value="ada@" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="f-email-hint f-email-error">
  <p id="f-email-hint" data-field="hint">We only use this to reply.</p>
  <p id="f-email-error" data-field="error">Error: enter an email address like name@example.com.</p>
</div>
```

#### Native validation

```html
<form action="#native-title" class="stack">
  <div data-field>
    <label for="f-code">Invite code</label>
    <input id="f-code" name="code" type="text" required minlength="6" aria-describedby="f-code-hint">
    <p id="f-code-hint" data-field="hint">Six characters or more.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="cluster">
    <button type="submit">Join</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

#### A group with an error

```html
<fieldset data-field aria-describedby="f-size-error">
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m"> Medium</label>
  <p id="f-size-error" data-field="error">Error: choose a size.</p>
</fieldset>
```

### Notes

Groups one control with its label, an optional hint and an optional error message, and styles the invalid state. The wiring is plain HTML and ARIA; this file only lays it out.

- The \<label for> names the control (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html> <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html> - Hint and error ids go in the control's aria-describedby, so they become its accessible description. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby> - When the value is wrong, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and show the error as text (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid> - Native constraint validation also gets the invalid look, via :user-invalid (only after the user has interacted). <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid>

Not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the error text starts with "Error:" (write it in the markup so every user and screen reader gets it), and an invalid control gets a thick start border as well as the danger color. Hide an error that does not apply with the hidden attribute and remove its id from aria-describedby.

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: The wiring is plain HTML and ARIA; this file only lays it out. - The \<label for> names the control (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html> <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html> - Hint and error ids go in the control's aria-describedby, so they become its accessible description. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby> - When the value is wrong, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and show the error as text (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid> - Native constraint validation also gets the invalid look, via :user-invalid (only after the user has interacted). <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid> Not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the error text starts with "Error:" (write it in the markup so every user and screen reader gets it), and an invalid control gets a thick start border as well as the danger color. Hide an error that does not apply with the hidden attribute and remove its id from aria-describedby.

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WCAG 3.3.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html)
- **WCAG 3.3.2**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)
- **WCAG 1.3.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)
- **MDN `aria-describedby`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby)
- **MDN `aria-invalid`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid)
- **MDN `:user-invalid`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid)

## Badge

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/badge.html

Inline status labels with tone variants that meet WCAG AA contrast.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/badge.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/badge.css):

```text
data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"
(empty means neutral)
```

`data-badge` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** badge tones are 8% of the tone mixed into the surface, with the tone as text. The tinted surfaces are derived tokens (`--dui-color-*-surface`), so a theme that changes the surface or a tone re-tints badges with no extra overrides.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/badge.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/badge.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/badge.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Tones

```html
<p class="cluster">
  <span data-badge>Draft</span>
  <span data-badge="accent">New</span>
  <span data-badge="success">Paid</span>
  <span data-badge="warning">Due soon</span>
  <span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span>
</p>
```

#### In context

```html
<table>
  <caption>Invoices</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col">Invoice</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>INV-031</td><td><span data-badge="success">Paid</span></td></tr>
    <tr><td>INV-032</td><td><span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

### Notes

A short inline status label ("Draft", "Paid", "Overdue"). Static text, not interactive: there is no native badge element and no ARIA role is needed, the text itself is the content. If a badge must be clickable, put a real \<button> or \<a href> around it, not a click handler on it. Native first: <https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1>

The tone is a hint, not the message: the words carry the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). If a badge sits next to something it labels only by position, say so in text, for example "Status: Paid" with .visually-hidden on "Status:". Text on each tone meets 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3); npm test checks every tone. <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Static text, not interactive: there is no native badge element and no ARIA role is needed, the text itself is the content. Native first: <https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1> The tone is a hint, not the message: the words carry the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). Text on each tone meets 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3); npm test checks every tone. <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WCAG 1.4.3**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- **WCAG 1.4.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)
- **Using ARIA rule 1**: [www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1](https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1)

### Source

- [`css/components/atoms/badge.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/badge.css)
- [`examples/atoms/badge.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/badge.html)
- [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md)

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent

## Molecules

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.html

Components use one `data-<component>` attribute each; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api). The levels follow [atomic design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/); planned [patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) are listed at their level with their status.

### Molecules

- [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md): Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes. Coming in M3.
- [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md): The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`. Coming in M3.
- [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md): A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface. Coming in M3.
- [Disclosure](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.md): A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`. Coming in M3.
- [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md): A button that opens a menu of actions. Coming in M3.
- [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md): Links to the pages of a long list of results. Coming in M3.
- [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md): Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute. Coming in M3.
- [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md): A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`. Coming in M3.
- [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md): Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs. Coming in M3.
- [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md): A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order. Coming in M3.
- [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md): A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short. Coming in M3.

## Organisms

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/organisms/index.html

Components use one `data-<component>` attribute each; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api). The levels follow [atomic design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/); planned [patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) are listed at their level with their status.

### Organisms

- [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md): A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport. Coming in M3.
- [Site navigation](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.md): The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked. Coming in M3.
- [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md): Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting. Coming in M3b.
- [Filter bar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.md): A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table. Coming in M3b.
- [Large forms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/large-forms.md): Long forms split into labelled groups, in one or more columns. Coming in M3b.

## Patterns

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.html

Where a standard exists, a native HTML element or a [WAI-ARIA APG pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/), the pattern follows it and links to it. Where none exists, the pattern is written as close to plain HTML as possible and labeled **Our choice:** with one line on why.

A pattern page fills in on its own when its example page or CSS file lands. Until then it says which milestone it is planned for. To go from a plain page to a full app step by step, read [From a simple site to an ERP app](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.md).

### M3: Molecules and navigation patterns

| Pattern | Level | Status | Follows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md) | molecule | Coming in M3 | [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/) |
| [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md) | molecule | Coming in M3 | [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/) |

| [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md) | molecule | Coming in M3 | **Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; a labelled `<nav>` with a list of links and `aria-current="page"` on the current one, as for breadcrumbs. |

| [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md) | molecule | Coming in M3 | [HTML `<search>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element), [MDN `<input type="search">`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search) |

## Alerts

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.html

Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes.

Coming in M3.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Note](https://vercel.com/geist/note)

## App shell

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.html

The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar.

**Our choice:** No standard defines an app shell; it is the HTML landmarks `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<aside>` placed with CSS grid, with no wrapper elements of our own.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

## Guides

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/index.html

- [From a simple site to an ERP app](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.md): Five steps from a plain content page to a dense business application, and which parts of each step are available today.

## From a simple site to an ERP app

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.html

Each step adds to the one before it, so a site can stop at any step. The lists below come from the [pattern registry](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) and show each pattern's status as of this build.

### Step 1: a plain content page

Write semantic HTML and link `css/domestic.css`. Headings, paragraphs, lists, links, tables, forms and `<dialog>` get their look from the base layer with no classes; see [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md). Arrange content with the layout primitives:

- [Cluster](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.md): An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).
- [Grid](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.md): A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.
- [Stack](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/stack.md): Vertical flow with a consistent gap between children.

Theme by overriding semantic tokens; see [Tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.md) and the [theming example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html).

### Step 2: site navigation

Add the main navigation, a breadcrumb trail and a search form:

- [Site navigation](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.md): The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked. Coming in M3.
- [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md): The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`. Coming in M3.
- [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md): A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`. Coming in M3.
- [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md): Links to the pages of a long list of results. Coming in M3.

None of these are available yet: Site navigation (M3), Breadcrumb (M3), Search (M3), Pagination (M3).

### Step 3: interactive widgets

Use a native element where one exists (`<details>`, `<dialog>`, `popover`, `<datalist>`), and an APG pattern where one does not:

- [Disclosure](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.md): A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`. Coming in M3.
- [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md): Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs. Coming in M3.
- [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md): A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport. Coming in M3.
- [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md): Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute. Coming in M3.
- [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md): A button that opens a menu of actions. Coming in M3.
- [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md): A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order. Coming in M3.
- [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md): A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short. Coming in M3.
- [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md): Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes. Coming in M3.
- [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md): A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface. Coming in M3.

None of these are available yet: Disclosure (M3), Tabs (M3), Dialog and drawer (M3), Popover (M3), Menu button (M3), Toolbar (M3), Typeahead (M3), Alerts (M3), Card (M3).

### Step 4: the app shell

Frame the application with a primary sidebar for navigation and an auxiliary sidebar for context, then lay out each screen as a list with details, a split view or a dashboard:

- [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md): The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar. Coming in M3b.
- [List-detail](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md): A list of items beside the details of the selected one, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.
- [Split](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md): Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.
- [Dashboard](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dashboard.md): A grid of summary sections, each with a heading, that reflows to fit the screen. Coming in M3b.

None of these are available yet: App shell (M3b), List-detail (M3b), Split (M3b), Dashboard (M3b).

### Step 5: data-heavy screens

Show records in a native `<table>`, narrow them with a filter bar, group long forms with `<fieldset>`, and switch to the compact density token where users scan a lot of data:

- [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md): Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting. Coming in M3b.
- [Filter bar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.md): A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table. Coming in M3b.
- [Large forms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/large-forms.md): Long forms split into labelled groups, in one or more columns. Coming in M3b.
- [Compact density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.md): A compact density token that tightens spacing for data-heavy screens. Coming in M3b.

None of these are available yet: Data table (M3b), Filter bar (M3b), Large forms (M3b), Compact density (M3b).

## Demos

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/demos.html

The same two views, a household-chores **dashboard** and an **account settings** form,
built four ways to show that domestic-ui works with plain HTML and with common frameworks.
Every view uses the same native markup, the `stack`, `cluster` and `grid` layout primitives, and
the [atom APIs](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md): `data-text`, `data-button`, `data-field`,
`data-badge` and the `role="switch"` checkbox, written exactly as in
[`examples/atoms/`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/index.html).

Each directory in [`demos/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos) with a `README.md`, by name, with the first sentence of that README. Demos are not part of this site; follow the link to read the source and how to run it.

- **Accessibility checker** ([`demos/a11y/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/a11y)): Checks the built demo apps the same way the repository checks `examples/`: Playwright with [axe](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) (tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`), in light and dark, with every `<details>` opened and checked again.
- **Angular** ([`demos/angular/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/angular)): The dashboard and account settings views in Angular 22: standalone components, two routes (`''` and `'settings'`) with Angular Router, a `title` per route, and `routerLinkActive` with `ariaCurrentWhenActive="page"` for the current link.
- **Astro** ([`demos/astro/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/astro)): The dashboard and account settings views as two static Astro pages (`src/pages/index.astro` and `src/pages/settings.astro`) sharing `src/layouts/Base.astro`.
- **React** ([`demos/react/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/react)): The dashboard and account settings views in React 19 with Vite, as a two-page [multi-page app](https://vite.dev/guide/build#multi-page-app) (`index.html` and `settings.html`).
- **Plain HTML** ([`demos/vanilla/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/vanilla)): The dashboard and account settings views as two static HTML files, with no build step.

## Contributing to domestic-ui

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/contributing.html

Rendered read-only from [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). To change it, [edit CONTRIBUTING.md on GitHub](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/edit/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Thanks for helping. This project is a design system built on native HTML, CSS tokens, and published web standards.

### Issues and pull requests

Use the issue forms for bugs and feature requests. Pull requests should use the template.

Branch names follow `fix/short-description`, `feat/short-description`, `docs/short-description`, or `a11y/short-description`.

#### Approval flow

Issues and pull requests from outside this repository's owners, members, or collaborators get the `needs-owen-approval` label automatically.

The maintainer approves an item by adding the `owen-approved` label. Only Owen applies that label. Team bots never apply `owen-approved` and never merge outside pull requests. Bots may merge their own pull requests.

An outside pull request cannot merge until the `owen-gate` check passes, which requires the `owen-approved` label.

`.github/CODEOWNERS` lists @odonckers on every file. That file is informational today: team bots push with the same GitHub account as Owen, so GitHub cannot tell his review apart from a bot's.

### Standards

- Prefer a native HTML element before adding a component or custom behavior.
- Cite the relevant [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/), [WHATWG](https://whatwg.org/), [W3C](https://www.w3.org/), [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), or [APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) documentation in the issue or pull request.
- If we choose a behavior the specs leave open, label it as our choice, not as a standard.
- Theme only through semantic `--dui-*` CSS custom properties. Do not hard-code colors, spacing, typography, or other design values in components.

The default theme should look complete and consistent out of the box. Consumers re-theme the system by overriding those tokens.

### Checks

`npm test` must pass. That run includes html-validate, axe, and stylelint.

### Changelog

Every user-facing change needs an entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Changelog

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/changelog.html

Rendered read-only from [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). To change it, [edit CHANGELOG.md on GitHub](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/edit/main/CHANGELOG.md).

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
Semantic token names and file paths under `css/` are public API; primitive tokens are not.

### [Unreleased]

#### Added

- `css/domestic.css`: zero-build entry point declaring
  `@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;` and importing each layer file.
- `reset` layer: a modest modern reset (`css/reset/reset.css`).
- `tokens` layer: primitive tokens (`css/tokens/primitives.css`) and semantic tokens
  (`css/tokens/semantic.css`), all prefixed `--dui-`, with `light-dark()` colors,
  a fluid `clamp()` type scale, spacing, radii, focus and motion tokens that collapse
  under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Theme scoping with `[data-theme]` or `.theme-*`, and scheme forcing with
  `data-color-scheme="light" | "dark"`.
- `base` layer: styles for text, links, lists, quotes, code, media, tables, form controls,
  buttons, `<dialog>`, `<details>`, visible `:focus-visible` and forced-colors support.
- `layout` layer: `.stack`, `.cluster` and `.grid` primitives configured with custom properties.
- `utilities` layer: `.visually-hidden`.
- Placeholders for `css/components/` and `web-components/`.
- `examples/base.html` and `examples/theming.html`.
- `PRINCIPLES.md`, including the semantic token reference.
- Tooling: html-validate, Stylelint, a token discipline check, and Playwright + axe-core
  accessibility tests in light and dark, all run by `npm test`.
- GitHub Actions: CI on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and a GitHub Pages skeleton.
- Atoms in `css/components/atoms/`, imported into the `components` layer, each with one attribute API:
  - Text helpers: `data-text="lead | small | muted"`.
  - Quiet link: `data-link="quiet"` (inherits text color, keeps its underline).
  - Buttons: `data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"` on `<button>`, `<input>`
    and `<a href>`; `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"` states; an inner focus ring on
    primary buttons. `type="submit"` stays primary by default.
  - Switch: `role="switch"` on `<input type="checkbox">`, per the APG Switch pattern, with
    forced-colors support.
  - Field: `data-field` with `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"`; invalid style for
    `aria-invalid="true"` and `:user-invalid`.
  - Badge: `data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`.
- Semantic tokens: `--dui-color-warning`, `--dui-color-accent-surface`, `--dui-color-success-surface`,
  `--dui-color-warning-surface`, `--dui-color-danger-surface`, `--dui-tint-amount`, `--dui-border-tint-amount`,
  `--dui-size-target-small`, `--dui-size-target-large` (and their primitives).
- `examples/atoms/`: an index and one page per atom; the theming example now shows atoms in both themes.
- Tests: atom states through Playwright accessibility APIs, rendered focus-ring contrast on every
  button variant, contrast pairs for every new token, and scoped theming of atoms.
- Firefox and WebKit Playwright projects alongside Chromium, installed in CI.

#### Fixed

- Base button hover and press styles no longer apply to buttons with `aria-disabled="true"`.
